findings.issue: Value list includes `CDS` at the top level; the schema digest's DataStandardEnum permits DICOM, BIDS, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, CDS, RO_CRATE, FHIR, OTHER — CDS is permitted, so this is valid. However the same slot is also populated on each FileCollection with `CDS` plus a modality standard, which is consistent. No defect; withdrawn on re-check.

`https://aireadi.org/` is used as an Organization identifier. The declared bundle contains no registry identifier for the AI-READI Consortium, and a project website URL is not an organization registry entry. Per the v5 identifier rule, an identifier naming something outside this dataset must come from the evidence or be omitted; the affiliation should carry only `name: AI-READI Consortium`.

The first creator entry represents the organizational creator (AI-READI Consortium, nameType Organizational, the sole DataCite creator) but embeds Aaron Lee as its `principal_investigator`, while a separate mechanism records him as central contact/responsible party in data_governance. This conflates the organizational creator with an individual and duplicates Aaron Lee's role. Aaron Lee should be his own Creator entry (as the other 15 PIs are) or omitted from the organizational entry.

Source commentary is placed on the first creator object where it describes the composition of the whole `creators` list ('The further creator entries below are...'). Per-object source_caveats annotates its own sibling slots, not the list; this commentary belongs in the top-level `source_caveats` or should be split so each statement annotates the object it concerns.

The Grant `id` is a NIH RePORTER search-permalink URL (`https://reporter.nih.gov/search/yatARMM-qUyKAhnQgsCTAQ/project-details/10885481`) and the `name` bundles the award number with the award title ('OT2OD032644: Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project'). The award number and the award title are distinct facts; embedding both in `name` and using a session-scoped search URL as the identifier degrades both. The other two grants carry bare award numbers in `name` with no id, so the list is internally inconsistent in shape.

Microsoft AI for Good Lab is recorded as a FundingMechanism with `grantor: Microsoft AI for Good Lab`. The bundle (Nature Metabolism acknowledgements) states only that the lab supported the cloud services needed for the project — an in-kind contribution, not a funding mechanism with a grantor relationship. The entry's own `notes` concedes this. Similarly the device manufacturers (Topcon, Optomed, iCare, Zeiss, Heidelberg, Dexcom, Garmin) provided loans and discounts and are correctly not listed as funders; Microsoft should be treated the same way and recorded in notes or collection_mechanisms rather than funders.

`data_substrate` is omitted while `data_topic` is populated. The bundle explicitly enumerates the substrates present (DICOM images, CSV/tabular, waveform data, time-series physiological data, questionnaire response data), several of which have exact B2AI_SUBSTRATE terms. Because a single Instance object cannot carry a list of substrates, omission is defensible, but the omission is not annotated anywhere; a source_caveats note on the instance would make the choice legible.

Only one Instance object is emitted for a dataset the bundle describes as spanning nine distinct datatypes with per-datatype file counts and standards. This is defensible (the healthsheet states each instance represents an individual patient) but the single object's `notes` carries the version-count history (204 / 1,067 / 2,280), which is version provenance belonging in `version_access` where it is already stated — a duplication across two slots.

The caveat states 'both are from the same tier 1 source, so both are represented here', but the two statements cited (healthsheet 'No' to demographic sub-populations; README split table reporting counts) are both within the FAIRhub API record — the same source, not two sources of equal tier. The disagreement is internal to one document and the caveat mischaracterizes it as a cross-source tie.

The `notes` field on most laboratory variables carries the reference range as prose ('Reference range: 3.6-5.2'), while VariableMetadata declares `minimum_value` and `maximum_value` as float-ranged slots. Where the bundle gives a numeric two-sided range (potassium 3.6-5.2, sodium 135-145, platelets 150-450, MCV 79-97, and roughly twenty others), those declared fields should be populated rather than restated in prose. Only `Montreal Cognitive Assessment total score` uses minimum_value/maximum_value.

For `Monofilament touch perception`, `categories` is a single-element list containing the string 'yes; no' — two category labels collapsed into one semicolon-joined value. A multivalued slot must carry one entry per distinct category: ['yes', 'no'].

Each FileCollection's `conforms_to` is written as a composed sentence naming two standards ('Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM), within a Clinical Data Structure (CDS) v0.1.1 directory layout'). The slot description asks for the standard the content follows; the composed phrasing is acceptable prose, but the top-level `conforms_to` already states the full mapping, so the nine per-collection restatements are largely redundant with it.

`restricted` is asserted where the only source statement is the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)'. The record's own source_caveats concedes that no source states the schema's terms and that the value is an inference from the access workflow. An enum value derived by inference from a differently-coded source is a claim the bundle does not make; omission would be the safer answer, with the HL7 code recorded in notes.

`compliant` is likewise inferred. The bundle states that the data were checked for HIPAA-identifiable content and that deIdentHIPAA is true, but never characterizes the dataset's HIPAA compliance status in the schema's terms. The accompanying caveat acknowledges this. This is an unsupported enum selection.

`false` is asserted on the basis of eligibility criteria, but the bundle records that the project engaged the Native Biodata Consortium regarding American Indian and Alaska Native communities, and the RO-Crate names no at-risk group. More materially, the boolean is asserted while the record's own source_caveats states the IRB questions on protected populations are unanswered in the bundle. A boolean the evidence does not settle should be omitted rather than inferred.

The top-level `license` string reads 'AI-READI Data License Agreement (Version 2.0)'. FAIRhub's landing page labels it 'Health Data License' and the FAIRhub API rights entry names it 'AI-READI custom license v2.0'; both are tier 1, and the license document (tier 2) supplies the value used. Preferring a tier 2 document title over two tier 1 metadata records inverts the declared ranking. The disagreement is disclosed in source_caveats, but the higher-ranked value should have been stated.

`publisher` has declared range `uriorcurie` and carries `https://fairhub.io/`. The bundle gives publisherName 'FAIRhub' with no registry identifier for that organization, so a bare website URL is standing in for an identifier the evidence does not supply. FAIRhub is also already recorded as the distribution platform elsewhere; the slot would be better omitted than filled with a homepage.
`created_by` repeats 'AI-READI Consortium', which is already the sole DataCite creator recorded in `creators[0].affiliations[0].name`. Not incorrect, but duplicative of structured content.

Omitted although the FAIRhub API supplies `created_at: 1763366400` (2025-11-17) for the dataset record. `issued` carries the same date, so the omission is defensible, but the field is available in the bundle.

Omitted. The bundle supplies https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access as the access route and the RO-Crate gives contentUrl https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3. Neither is a direct data download (access is gated behind login and licence acceptance), so omission is correct — but the access route appears only inside distribution_formats[0].access_urls and data_governance prose, which is the right placement and should be confirmed as deliberate.

Omitted while `related_datasets` records is_new_version_of relations to fairhub.1 and fairhub.2. The bundle states v3.0.0 contains the pilot, year-2 and year-3 data cumulatively, so derivation from prior versions is arguably supported; the typed relationships already capture this, so the omission is defensible but undocumented.

Omitted. The bundle's healthsheet answers 'No' to whether the dataset has been used for any tasks already, and FAIRhub reports cited: 0. Omission is the correct treatment of a negative answer (a slot should not be populated with 'none'), but the FAIRhub view count of 24,636 is unrecorded anywhere.
Omitted. The healthsheet answers 'No' to whether a repository links to papers or systems that use the dataset. Correctly omitted; noted for completeness of the audit.

Omitted. The healthsheet's erratum question has an empty response string. Omission is correct — an empty source answer is not evidence of an erratum — but it is one of three healthsheet questions left blank in the source (erratum, de-identification measures, de-identification preprocessing), and that pattern is not noted in source_caveats.

Omitted although the bundle states plainly that 'currently there is no mechanism for others to extend or augment the AI-READI dataset outside of those who are involved in the project'. This is a substantive governance fact; ExtensionMechanism has no required keys and `extension_details` could carry it. Arguably a supported omission under the rule against populating a slot with an absence, but the fact is then lost entirely.

Omitted while `prohibited_uses` carries seven entries. The healthsheet's question about discouraged applications is answered by reference to the licence restrictions, which are recorded as prohibitions. The routing is defensible (licence terms are prohibitions, not discouragements), but no discouraged-use content is recorded and the choice is unannotated.

Omitted. The bundle states the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic and intended to facilitate multiple potential downstream AI/ML applications, which arguably supports an OtherTask entry; the content is instead folded into `tasks` and `intended_uses`. Acceptable routing, noted for completeness.

All three omitted. The bundle repeatedly answers 'N/A - no labels are provided' and 'N/A - no labeling was performed'. Omission is correct per the rule against recording an absence as a value; the fact that no labeling was performed is captured in `instances[0].label: false` and `label_description`, which is the right placement.
Omitted. The bundle states no imputation is described, and `missing_data_documentation[0].handling_strategy` records that no imputation was applied. Correctly omitted.

Omitted although the healthsheet explicitly answers 'No, a data protection impact analysis has not been conducted.' Omission is correct treatment of a negative, consistent with the handling of errata and existing_uses.

Both omitted. The FAIRhub API records `parent: null` and `child: 4` for this dataset, and the landing page notes 'A smaller version is available for pipeline development'. The mini-subset is recorded only in top-level `notes`; it could support a `related_datasets` entry, but the bundle gives it no DOI or identifier, so a DatasetRelationship (which requires `target_dataset`) is not constructible. Omission is therefore forced, and the notes placement is the correct fallback.

The caveat correctly discloses the 2023-07-19 vs 18 July 2023 discrepancy and states the tier-1 FAIRhub value was preferred. The same discrepancy is restated in the top-level `source_caveats` item (5). Duplication across two levels; one statement would suffice.

Each ExternalResource object carries a single string in the `external_resources` field formatted as 'Label: URL'. The slot name is plural and the field accepts the resource description; the label-colon-URL concatenation is readable but mixes a human label with a locator in one string across all nine entries.

The list merges the FAIRhub dataset keywords (Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam) with the study-description keywords (Type 2 Diabetes, Data Sharing, Exploratory Data Collection). Both sets are in the bundle and both are tier 1, so the merge is supported; noted because the merged list no longer corresponds to either source's keyword field as stated.

summary: Audited the full record against the declared bundle (AI_READI_preprocessed.txt, md5 8abd7bf5389b562b95794d656af19392) and the Dataset slot digest. The record is broadly well-grounded: the 2,280-participant count, 356,343 files, 3,815,969,779,678 bytes, the nine datatype directories with their per-directory file counts and byte sizes, the 70/15/15 split table, the licence terms, the IRB protocol number, and the version history are all traceable to tier 1 sources, and the extensive top-level source_caveats correctly discloses nine cross-source disagreements. Findings cluster in five areas. (1) Identifier hygiene: a project homepage stands in as an Organization id for the AI-READI Consortium, a session-scoped RePORTER search URL serves as a Grant id, and `publisher` holds a website URL in a uriorcurie slot where the bundle supplies only a name. (2) Structural collapse in multivalued or typed fields: `categories` holds 'yes; no' as one string instead of two entries; roughly twenty laboratory variables carry two-sided numeric reference ranges as prose in `notes` while the declared `minimum_value`/`maximum_value` float slots sit empty. (3) Inferred enum values: `confidentiality_level: restricted` and `hipaa_compliant: compliant` are both derived by inference from differently-coded source statements, as their own caveats concede, and `at_risk_groups_included: false` is asserted where the record simultaneously states the governing IRB questions are unanswered in the bundle. (4) Ranking inversion: `license` prefers the tier 2 licence-document title over two tier 1 FAIRhub labels; the disagreement is disclosed but the declared ranking was not followed. (5) Entity conflation and misclassification: the organizational creator entry embeds an individual PI and carries list-level commentary in its per-object source_caveats, and the Microsoft AI for Good Lab cloud-services acknowledgement is recorded as a FundingMechanism with a grantor when the bundle describes only in-kind support. Omissions were checked individually: `existing_uses`, `use_repository`, `errata`, `data_protection_impacts`, `imputation_protocols`, and the three labeling slots are all correctly omitted in response to explicit negative or N/A answers in the healthsheet, and `parent_datasets`/`resources` are forced omissions because the mini-subset has no identifier in the bundle. The one omission that loses substantive content is `extension_mechanism`, where the bundle states plainly that no mechanism exists for outside contribution. No fabricated facts were found; no value was traced to any source outside the declared bundle.
